audience.text: Go developers building applications that need to generate, read, or modify Excel spreadsheets programmatically without external native dependencies.

capabilities.text: Read and write cell values using A1-style references with Cells.Get and Cells.Set, supporting string, float64, int, and bool types.
capabilities.title: Cell data read/write

capabilities.text: Store formulas with Cell.SetFormula and evaluate them using CalculateFormula, supporting 22 functions, arithmetic, comparison, and cross-sheet references.
capabilities.title: Formula evaluation

capabilities.text: Apply font, fill, alignment, border, and number format settings via Style objects and Cell.SetStyle, with automatic style deduplication on save.
capabilities.title: Styling and formatting

capabilities.text: Support merged cells, freeze panes, auto-filters, row/column insert/delete, column widths, row heights, and hyperlinks.
capabilities.title: Worksheet layout features

capabilities.text: Create and manage structured tables, data validation rules, conditional formatting (color scales, data bars, icon sets, top-N), and pivot tables.
capabilities.title: Structured data features

capabilities.text: Add charts (bar, line, pie, scatter, area) with axis titles and legends, and embed PNG or JPEG pictures into worksheets.
capabilities.title: Charting and embedding

capabilities.text: Export workbooks to CSV with Workbook.ExportToCSV and import CSV with Workbook.ImportFromCSV, supporting custom delimiters and type inference.
capabilities.title: CSV import/export

capabilities.text: Read and write workbooks from any io.Reader/io.Writer, including HTTP responses, zip entries, and network streams, using LoadFrom, SaveTo, and StreamingReader.
capabilities.title: Streaming and I/O

limitations.text: Cell references are A1-style strings only; tuple/array indices are not supported.
CalculateFormula supports 22 functions, arithmetic/comparison operators, and same-workbook cross-sheet references; external-workbook references and full Excel function library are not included.
Number formats use the 1900 date system only; 1904 date system is not supported.
Charts do not support 3D, combo charts, secondary axes, data labels, or gridline styling; pivot tables lack calculated fields, grouping, and custom aggregations.
Hidden rows/columns, outline grouping, print setup, and sheet protection are not modeled; VBA support is storage-only.
Modified content regenerates XML; unmodified content reuses original XML byte-for-byte on round-trip.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic Excel file creation and editing in Go using a pure-Go implementation with no third-party dependencies.
Supports low-memory streaming of large Excel files via row-by-row processing without loading the entire workbook into memory.
Provides a built-in formula engine to evaluate common Excel formulas and propagate error values like #DIV/0!.
Allows round-tripping of Excel workbooks with password protection using ECMA-376 Agile Encryption.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Cells FOSS for Go is a pure-Go library for creating, reading, and writing Excel workbooks in ECMA-376 Office Open XML formats with no third-party dependencies.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported formula functions beyond the 22 listed is not fully enumerated in the fact dossier.
Whether conditional formatting supports Excel 2010+ extensions like x14 gradient data bars is not confirmed by the fact dossier.
The behavior of InsertRow/DeleteRow on formula text rewriting is stated as not rewriting, but the full scope of range updates is not detailed.
The exact behavior of streaming reader when encountering malformed or unsupported cell types is not specified.
Whether the library supports .xlsm format beyond .xlsx is not explicitly confirmed in the fact dossier.
The exact encryption parameters for password-protected workbooks beyond SHA-512/AES-256-CBC are not detailed.
Whether the library supports embedded OLE objects beyond pictures is not specified.
The exact behavior of the formula engine on circular references is not documented in the fact dossier.

workflows.name: Create and save a workbook
workflows.text: Create a new workbook with NewWorkbook, access the first worksheet, write cell values using Cells.Set, and save to disk with Workbook.Save.

workflows.name: Load, modify, and save an existing workbook
workflows.text: Load an existing workbook with LoadWorkbook, read a cell value with Cell.AsString, update it with Cells.Set, and save the modified workbook.

workflows.name: Stream large Excel files row-by-row
workflows.text: Use NewStreamingReader to process large Excel files with ProcessRows, accumulating totals or filtering data without loading the full workbook into memory.

workflows.name: Apply styles and formatting
workflows.text: Create Style objects with font, fill, alignment, and border settings, then apply them to cells using Cell.SetStyle.

workflows.name: Import data from CSV
workflows.text: Import data from a CSV file into a new workbook using Workbook.ImportFromCSV, specifying the delimiter and target sheet name.

workflows.name: Add data validation rules
workflows.text: Create a DataValidation object with type, formula, and error settings, then add it to a worksheet range using Worksheet.AddDataValidation.
